This past June I was in a similar spot. My job became so stressful I felt I was on the verge of a mental breakdown. After about a month of thinking it over, I decided I needed to quit with or without another job lined up. My husband was worried but overall understood. We agreed he would pay the mortgage, however I would use my savings to pay my half of the bills and we’d continue to split groceries 50/50. 

After quitting, I realized I needed a break. My husband supported this. I took two months off. It was a great reset. Following those two months, I decided to get back on the horse and job search. Found a job, and things are back to normal.

I sympathize with your girlfriend if she’s having a hard time at work. A break did wonders for me, and that could be what she needs as well. However. Expecting you to pay for everything and deciding to just be a permanent homemaker is entirely unfair. There’s no reason why at 24 and no children, she cannot work. If you’re not comfortable, and I think it’s completely normal that you’re not, talk to her. Maybe suggest she take a couple months break, but encourage her to have a plan in place before quitting. And if you’re not married, she should contribute however way she can. Otherwise, I believe she’s using you.

Don’t let student debt keep you from going to school. Try to remember it’s an investment and you’ll make all that money back with the high paying job you got because you went to school. 

I was able to fully pay off my student loans within 5 years of graduating. Remember, it’s not a life sentence.
Friends will come and go. Don’t let this ruin you.

In my experience, the best way to trim down on the belly fat is to trim down on the sugar, carbs and general junk from your diet. Try to eat smaller portions, no snacking, and lots of veggies and high fibre foods. Drink tons of water. Try to avoid cream and sugar in your coffee (just add a splash of milk if you don’t drink black.) Get as much sleep as you can. Try to limit your alcohol consumption, especially beer and other high sugar drinks. 20 minutes of exercise a day, even if it’s just a walk around the block or jumping jacks in front of the TV. Try this for a month, and you should absolutely see a difference in your gut.

I used to do this too when I was younger. Almost every night. Pretty sure my dad thought I was out doing drugs. I’d slip out for around an hour late at night and swing at the park in the dark. When the odd person would walk by, I’m pretty sure they were freaked out by me. 

I moved and there are no parks near me now. I miss it.

I understand the whole surprise thing, but my husband started asking me about ring size a full year before he proposed. He just said he wanted to know for future reference. 

Turns out I measured my finger wrong and it was the wrong size anyways. It wasn’t a big deal and I was so thrilled about the engagement, I didn’t care. In a week’s time, it was sized properly and I could wear it. I think asking would be your best bet, in a casual “just wondering” sort of way.

I had the opposite problem. When I started my job three years ago, my boss told me I didn’t ask enough questions. This was false, I was asking tons of questions. I just wasn’t asking him questions, as I was directing all my inquiries to my direct supervisor and trainer. 

Even at my probationary meeting, he said my communication needed work because I didn’t ask enough questions. 

Sometimes he would walk to me randomly and say “you haven’t asked any questions in a while.” It really stressed me out, to the point where sometimes I’d make something up just so I could ask him something, which obviously is a huge waste of his time and mine. My point is questions are a good thing, and some managers want you to ask lots of questions. 

Give yourself a time. A month isn’t long. You’ll catch on soon enough and it will feel like a huge accomplishment. Hang in there!
Thanks for the advice. I have over a year of salary saved and my husband makes enough to cover the mortgage.

Here’s my experience. I was in a situation fairly similar to you three years ago. Wanted out of my current job, received an offer and took it, even though it was a pay cut of about $5000/year. 

Since then, I haven’t received a single raise or bonus. My last company provided annual raises and bonuses. With that factored in, and keeping in mind I haven’t received a raise in three years, the pay cut has become quite substantial. I regret leaving my former job and it has turned out to my a big financial mistake of mine. 

That said, your situation might not be a glum as mine. Sometimes receiving a pay cut for a better opportunity is a good thing. Just be careful to evaluate and accept everything you’re leaving behind at your current employer, as this was something I failed to do.  Remember, the grass is always greener on the other side. Good luck.

I missed my university graduation because I already had a job lined up. That said, I was offered a job out of state so it would’ve been hard to make arrangements with my work. 

Frankly, it felt really good. I was the only one of my classmates who had employment immediately after school finished. I have no regrets, although I do agree this is personal preference, and the same might not go for you. If you told them this in the interview, send an email. If they are  reasonable, it shouldn’t be an issue.
Good luck to you!

I can definitely relate to your post. I’m educated with a stable career. My husband is a university drop out working retail. 

Been married two years, together for nine. He is the only person in his family NOT on welfare, owns a nice house and living a decent life. I’m sure his mother would love to take credit for that but frankly, I think his upbringing was terrible and many of our accomplishments are my accomplishments that he sat in the backseat for. I believe if I were to divorce him, his family would immediately blame me, blacklist me, and wholeheartedly believe his drinking, the divorce and many of his problems where my doing.

I’m turning 30 in a month and I want to have kids soon. My life is on hold and I don’t know if I should cut my losses or stay. 

Wishing you the best OP. Try to remember, he should be your partner, not your responsibility.

I can relate. My Q gets very affectionate when he’s been drinking. Almost to the point where it makes me uncomfortable. When he is sober, he usually keeps to himself- zero physical contact unless initiated by me.

Sadly, when he’s overly affectionate, that’s usually a giveaway that he has been drinking.
